text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are suffering from severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria; to begin my assessment, can you tell me exactly where you feel the most intense pain and how long these symptoms have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) with secondary cystitis.

The patient's history of dysuria, post-coital pain, and severe abdominal cramping in a sexually active female is highly suggestive of an ascending genital infection. Given the severity and duration of the symptoms, I am requesting a Urinalysis and a Pelvic Ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis and rule out tubo-ovarian abscess.
